Q: Python Error: InsertError: replace() argument 2 must be str, not None A:

You can use <variable> if <variable> is not None else '', however, you'd have to write that for every variable in your code because you're repeating yourself; you should refactor your code.

I'll use a dict to hold the placeholders and values, then replace each one in a loop.

replacements = {
    "%TRACKINGNO%": TrackingNo,
    "%COURIER%": CourierName,
    "%ORDERNO%": OrderNo,
    "%TRACKURL%": URL,
    "%DESPATCHEDDATE%": DespatchedDate,
    "%NAME%": PostalName,
    "%POSTCODE%": PostCode,
}

# ...

with open ("D:\Scripts\html.html", "r") as htmlfile:
    html = htmlfile.read()

filled_html = html  # For first loop
for placeholder, value in replacements.items():
    filled_html = filled_html.replace(
        placeholder,
        value if value is not None else '')

Q: Cloudformation: Why does RDS instance creates default security group when i am already creating one while initating RDS? A:

I can't exactly explain why a default security group is created and overlap with the one you specified. What I can tell you though is that you should really rely on VPCSecurityGroups which replaces the old DBSecurityGroups which was relevant in "EC2 Classic" (before the VPC era). Perhaps this will solve the issue.

There's an article in the doc to learn more about this: http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.RDSSecurityGroups.html#Overview.RDSSecurityGroups.Compare.

Q: Execute update statement in Azure Data Factory A:

Try to wrap your code in dynamic content with concat function something like this.

@concat('UPDATE MPH_CATALOG_DEV.MPH_STAGE_SCHEMA.MPH_TABLE_REFRESH_LOOKUP
    SET ACTIVE = 0 WHERE
    TARGET_TABLE_SCHEMA = ',item().TARGET_TABLE_SCHEMA,' and
    TARGET_TABLE_NAME   = ',item().TARGET_TABLE_NAME,' ;
select 0 as id;')

Q: Set upstream branch without using `git push` A:

Try this command:

git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/main

You can see it at work in the following repository with 2 remotes:

$ git remote -v | grep push
origin  git@codeberg.org:razzi/.dotfiles.git (push)
sourcehut   git@git.sr.ht:~razzi/.dotfiles (push)

# Currently, origin is the upstream
$ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream}
origin/main

# However I can change it without pushing:
$ git branch --set-upstream-to=sourcehut/main
branch 'main' set up to track 'sourcehut/main'.

# now it pushes to the other one, sourcehut, by default (I use -v to show the name)
$ git push -v
Pushing to git.sr.ht:~razzi/.dotfiles
...
Everything up-to-date

Q: Changing column values based on values of separate columns A:

You can define a separation list seps and then use cut like below

seps <- list(brown = c(3, 6), rainbow = c(3, 5), coho = c(2, 6))

df %>%
    mutate(
        age = cut(Length_in,
            c(-Inf, seps[[Species[1]]], Inf),
            labels = c("Yoy", "Age1", "Age2+")
        ), .by = Species
    )
